informal_statement:
Let \(a<b\), let
\[
F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R
\]
be continuous on \([a,b]\), and suppose
\[
F(a)>V>F(b).
\]
There exists \(r\in(a,b)\) with
\[
F(r)=V,
\]
greatest in \([a,b]\cap F^{-1}(\{V\})\), and
\[
F(t)<V
\]
for \(r<t\leq b\).
reason: Source `GreatestLevelRoot.lean:12-48`: The strict opposite endpoint inequalities yield a greatest interior level point and a strict barrier on the half-open interval to its right; uniqueness is not assumed.
